intro: Every conversation runs on questions. Who is the new student? Where is the bathroom? When is the party? How much does the empanada cost? In this unit you learn the small Spanish words that start those questions: quién, qué, dónde, cuándo, por qué, cómo and cuánto.

Each question word asks for one kind of answer. Quién wants a person. Dónde wants a place. Cuándo wants a time. You will learn to spot the accent mark that every question word carries, and to tell por qué (why) from porque (because).

Then you put the words to work. You will interview a classmate, answer in full sentences and use polite words like por favor, gracias, de nada and perdón. By the end, you can ask and answer the questions people use when they first meet.
bigQuestion: How do questions help us get to know people and find out what we need?

timeline.t: Learn ¿quién?, ¿qué? and ¿cómo? to ask about people and things
Learn ¿dónde?, ¿cuándo? and ¿cuánto? to ask about places, times and amounts
Spot the written accent on every question word
Ask about any part of a sentence with the right question word
Ask a classmate's name, age and home
Listen for the question word and answer in a full sentence
Use por favor, gracias, de nada and perdón
Plan and carry out a short interview in Spanish

words.d: who? — asks about a person: ¿Quién es?
what? — asks about a thing or action: ¿Qué haces?
where? — asks about a place: ¿Dónde está el baño?
when? — asks about a time or day: ¿Cuándo es la fiesta?
why? — two words with an accent: ¿Por qué estás triste?
because — one word, no accent: Porque estoy cansado.
how? or what is it like? — ¿Cómo estás? ¿Cómo es tu perro?
how much? — ¿Cuánto cuesta? (How much does it cost?)
What is your name? — answer: Me llamo…
How old are you? — answer with tener: Tengo nueve años.
you are welcome — the answer to gracias
sorry or excuse me — Perdón, ¿dónde está la biblioteca?

test.q: Which question word asks about a place?

test.why: The question why is two words with an accent: por qué.

test.q: What does ¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños? mean?
test.why: ¿Cuándo? asks when, and el cumpleaños is the birthday.

test.q: Which answer to ¿Cuántos años tienes? is correct?

test.why: Flor is feminine, so how many is cuántas.

test.q: Someone says Gracias. What is the best reply?
test.why: De nada means you are welcome.

test.q: Which is the best full-sentence answer to ¿Vives en Chicago?
test.why: Change the tú ending -es to the yo ending -o: vivo.

test.q: What does ¿Cómo es tu maestra? ask?
test.why: ¿Cómo es…? asks what someone is like.

test.q: Which question is polite for a new principal?
test.why: Use usted with an adult at school.

test.q: Sentence: Diego lee en la biblioteca. Which question asks about the person?
test.why: ¿Quién? asks who, so it replaces the person, Diego.

test.q: Why does como in Como arroz have no accent?
choices: It means I eat, not how.
It is at the start of the sentence.
test.why: Cómo with an accent asks how; como without one is a form of comer.

test.q: In the empanada story, who ate the last empanada?
test.why: Lupe followed the crumbs to the dog, Canela.

test.q: You did not understand a question. What can you say?
test.why: Otra vez, por favor asks someone to say it again.

test.q: Which question has the usual Spanish word order?
test.why: Spanish puts the verb right after the question word.

test.q: Which is correct for thank you very much?
test.why: Muchas matches gracias, which is feminine and plural.

write.prompt: Escribe una entrevista. Write 4–6 lines in Spanish: a greeting, three or four questions with different question words (like ¿Cómo te llamas?, ¿Dónde vives?, ¿Cuántos años tienes?) with a full-sentence answer to each, and a polite thank-you at the end.
tips: Start each question with ¿ and end it with ?.
Put the accent on every question word: qué, quién, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto.
Answer with the yo form of the verb: tengo, vivo, me llamo.
Use tú with a classmate and usted with an adult.
Read your interview aloud with a partner.
